CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling in bilateral hands

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 60-year-old right-handed male referred for evaluation of numbness and tingling in bilateral hands. Symptoms began several weeks after a motor vehicle accident in December during which he sustained bilateral wrist fractures. Since his fractures healed, he has noted progressive tingling and numbness, with worsening over the past month. The right wrist was more severely injured than the left. He describes symptoms as primarily soreness with occasional throbbing and associated weakness, particularly with hand use. Tingling is more prominent when painful and becomes dull when pain resolves. Symptoms are most noticeable at night and wax and wane throughout the day. Denies true loss of sensation but reports decreased sensitivity. He was prescribed nerve pain medication but has not been taking it consistently. He wears splints on both wrists, predominantly on the right, which provides relief. Also reports mild neck stiffness since hitting his head during the accident with documented contusion at that time. Right-hand symptoms extend from the middle and ring fingers up the forearm. Left-hand symptoms extend from the pinky and ring fingers.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: fatigue and weight gain
Eyes: floaters
GI: excessive appetite and bloating
Cardiovascular: shortness of breath and leg swelling
Endocrine: constant hunger
Skin: nail bed changes, dryness, and itching
Musculoskeletal: gout and muscle pain
Remainder of systems reviewed and negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Motor vehicle accident with bilateral wrist fractures (December)
Head contusion
Prediabetes (controlled with dietary modification)

MEDICATIONS
Coreg for hypertension
Lexapro for anxiety
Nerve pain medication (prescribed but non-compliant with dosing)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Right-handed
Recent motor vehicle accident in December

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic examination reveals:
Right hand: Sensation normal except diminished pin prick sensation in third and fourth fingers
Left hand: Decreased sensation in fourth and fifth fingers
Reflexes: 1+ and symmetric upper extremities, 2+ in knees, toes downgoing bilaterally
Tinel sign: Positive at both wrists and both elbows
Remainder of examination: Normal

RESULTS
Clinical examination findings consistent with bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome or bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome. EMG testing scheduled to pinpoint exact location of nerve irritation.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, most likely etiology given symptom distribution and history of bilateral wrist trauma, with differential diagnosis of bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome.

1. Schedule EMG/NCS testing to determine exact location of nerve compression
2. Follow-up visit after test completion to review results
3. Continue wearing bilateral wrist splints
4. If symptoms persist after testing, consider referral to hand clinic for injections or carpal tunnel release surgery, or alternative referral to orthopedics
5. Reinforce importance of taking nerve pain medication as prescribed
